title: Security officials warn the US aviation industry of recent calls for attack by Al Qaeda | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

US security agencies are warning commercial airlines, air cargo carriers and airports around the nation of recent public messaging by terrorists calling for attacks similar to September’s attempted hijacking by the pilot of aTel Aviv-bound Flydubai flight.

On Thursday, the FBI, Department of Homeland Security and Transportation Security Administration jointly sent an informational report to members of the aviation industry indicating affiliates of Al Qaeda and the terror group’s supporters “have released multiple messages praising the attempted hijacking and encouraging similar attacks against perceived US, Israeli, and Jewish interests,” according to a copy of the report obtained by CNN.

There are no known specific and credible threats underway, a law enforcement source told CNN, adding that security officials routinely share items of concern with private industry that are detected by the US intelligence community.

The FBI declined to comment. CNN has reached out to the TSA for comment.

The notice comes ahead of the busiest travel week of the year. AAA anticipates about 6 million people will travel by air on US domestic flights from November 24 to November 30.

The recent terror group messaging “reiterates longstanding AQ narratives that encourage supporters to exploit aviation access, evade security measures, and conduct attacks using commercial aircraft,” the report to the aviation industry said.

The report provided various examples of recent public messaging by Al Qaeda-affiliated leaders and media outlets celebrating the attempted hijacking.

Several messages have “praised the attempted Flydubai hijacking as a model for bypassing security measures and encouraged supporters to emulate the attack and target US and Jewish interests worldwide,” the report said.

In September,a pilot on a Dubai-to-Tel Avivflight was arrested after he stabbed the other pilot in the cockpit with an ax during an apparent attempt to crash the plane, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

Despite being wounded, Netanyahu told CNN the attacked pilot fought back and “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster.”

Sources said the attacker,Hamam al-Hammami,had terrorist images on his social media.

“Although individuals inspired by foreign terrorist organizations (FTOs) historically have not mobilized to violence directly in response to FTO calls for action,” Thursday’s warning to the aviation industry said, “they have demonstrated the ability to mobilize rapidly and with little or no warning.

The report noted that recent praise of the attempted Flydubai by terrorist affiliates, as well as ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, “could exacerbate existing grievances against the United States” and mobilize terrorist sympathizers to violence.

The report also included a series of potential indicators by people who may be planning an attack that the airline industry should be on guard against, and encouraged aviation officials to promptly contact law enforcement with any concerns.

Those possible red flags included: individuals seeking to avoid security procedures; people without a legitimate business reason asking the aviation industry for detailed information about flight operations and security procedures; individuals expressing “a strong desire to handle specific items of luggage” without assistance; as well as the unexplained loss of items like airline radios, access badges, and uniforms.
